## Rule

ARC-GEN source: `external/ARC-GEN/tasks/task_77fdfe62.py`.

Generator emits a square input of side `size+4`, where `size in {2,4,6}`. A blue frame sits at row/col `1` and `size+2`; the four outer corners `(0,0)`, `(0,size+3)`, `(size+3,0)`, `(size+3,size+3)` hold four distinct non-blue/non-cyan colors. Cyan cells inside the inner `size x size` square at offset `(2,2)` are recolored by quadrant:
- top-left cyan -> top-left corner color
- top-right cyan -> top-right corner color
- bottom-left cyan -> bottom-left corner color
- bottom-right cyan -> bottom-right corner color

The output is the compact `size x size` grid. Cyan cells become their quadrant color, non-cyan in-grid cells are black `0`, and padding outside the compact output is empty/all-zero in NeuroGolf encoding.

## Algorithm sketch

```python
size = input_side - 4
colors = [grid[0][0], grid[0][size+3], grid[size+3][0], grid[size+3][size+3]]
out = zeros(size, size)
for r, c in cyan_pixels_shifted_by_minus_2:
    q = (r >= size // 2) * 2 + (c >= size // 2)
    out[r][c] = colors[q]
```

ONNX `coloridx_einsum`: free-input Einsum reads `size` and the four corner color ids as scalars; a 6x6 UINT8 color-index canvas is assembled with `Where`; non-cyan active cells are `0`, inactive cells are sentinel `10`; `Equal(color_idx, ids[0..9])` expands the small one-hot, and `Pad` writes the free graph output.

## 2026-06-21 w01 visual/scratch note

Visual pass matches `external/ARC-GEN/tasks/task_77fdfe62.py`: output is compact `size x size`, where `size in {2,4,6}` and input side is `size+4`. Blue is only the frame; cyan marks source cells; the four non-blue/non-cyan outer corners provide quadrant colors TL/TR/BL/BR. Black `0` is a real in-grid output color for non-cyan cells, while only off-grid padding is empty/all-zero.

ARC-GEN falsifications checked: this is not an inner crop of the input because cyan cells are recolored from corner colors and non-cyan cells become black; it is not a single foreground-color rule because one output can contain all four distinct corner colors; it is not safe to treat black output cells as padding/sentinel.

## 2026-06-22 w-183 dissolve floor proof (no-candidate; 839 re-confirmed)

Re-measured team-best `../K-NeuroGolf-OnnxlyFans/Team_Submission/Backend/Team_Best_Onnx/task183.onnx`
= **839** (memory 760 + params 79), score_v2 + profile_real_cost `--arcgen 266` profile==static==839
(fully static graph ⇒ local == Kaggle exact), visible 265/265, truth-full 200000/200000. It IS the
`pad18_axes` graph. (No `staged_submits/task183_*` exists in this worktree; the prompt's staged path
is another worker's tree — re-scored the team-best directly.)

`largest_intermediate` breakdown of the 760 memory: **360 B `onehot6 [1,10,6,6]` BOOL** (Equal output,
47.4%), **144 B `cyan_f32 [1,1,6,6]` F32** (Slice, 18.9%), then ~36 B U8/BOOL working tensors + tiny
scalars. Both top tensors are forced (proofs below).

**The dissolve target priced and KILLED — the 360 B one-hot CANNOT become a scorer-invisible in-kernel temp.**
The blocker is the cyan scatter rank. Measured on 400 fresh ARC-GEN pairs: cyan-mask matrix rank
distribution `{1:91, 2:74, 3:75, 4:51, 5:65, 6:44}`, **mean 3.14, full-rank-6 in 11% of cases**. The
cyan pattern is arbitrary random pixels — NOT low-rank-separable — so a #109 free-output multi-term
Einsum needs **one term per cell (T=36)**, and a runtime rank-decomposition is impossible (Loop/Unique
banned). Per-cell free-output prices (selectors are F32-LOCKED — #109 carrier tax, confirmed by this
task's own ORT-rejected F16 Einsum probes):

| dissolve route | priced bytes (replaces 360 B one-hot) | verdict |
|---|---:|---|
| #109 free-output Einsum, write 30×30 direct: `R,C [36,30] F32 + K [36,10] F32` | 4320+4320+1440 = **10080 B** | LOSES by ~9700 |
| #109 free-output Einsum, write 6×6 then Pad: `R,C [36,6] F32 + K [36,10] F32` | 864+864+1440 = **3168 B** | LOSES by ~2800 |
| #116 direct OneHot, indices padded to `[1,1,30,30]` U8 (+ off-grid sentinel) | 900 B (min) | LOSES (vs 360) |
| #116 OneHot at `[1,1,6,6]` index → `[1,10,6,6]` → Pad | 360 B (identical to current Equal-tail) | no gain (== current) |
| Angle-3 `Equal(padded_idx[1,1,30,30] U8, ids[10])` value canvas | 900 B | LOSES (already in kill table) |

Why the in-kernel-temp dissolve (#89/#188) does not transfer here: that lever works when the mask is a
SEPARABLE row⊗col outer product (task188 stripes) or a handful of rank-1 channel terms (task234 solid
boxes). task183's per-channel output mask is an arbitrary full-rank-up-to-6 cyan scatter routed to 4
data-dependent color channels; expressing it free-output forces T=36 explicit rank-1 terms whose F32
selectors (3168–10080 B) dwarf the 360 B one-hot they delete. The 360 B `onehot6` IS the minimal
materialization.

**Forced-component proof (both top tensors):**
- 360 B one-hot: output contract is `[1,10,30,30]` (10 channels). Reachable colors are 8 (`{0,2,3,4,5,6,7,9}`;
  blue 1 / cyan 8 never output) but an 8-channel tail must channel-Pad back to 10 (zero channels at 1 and 8),
  re-materializing the same 360 B. Max output 6×6 is generator-pinned (`size=6` test), so the spatial tail
  cannot shrink below 6×6, and `10·6·6 = 360 B` is the #81/#116 small-grid floor (below the ~90-cell crossover
  where 30×30 canvas would cost 900 B). DEAD.
- 144 B F32 cyan slice: `Slice(input, ch8) [1,1,6,6] F32`. Gate harness feeds F32 (§INPUT-DTYPE-LOCK), so the
  one-channel cyan read at the 6×6 inner extent is F32; F16 cast keeps the F32 slice live and costs MORE
  (probe `f16cyan` = 1070, killed). DEAD.

**The ONE lever that could still break 839** (none found this session): a representation that needs neither
the `[1,10,6,6]` one-hot NOR an F32 cyan read — e.g. if the validator's decoder accepted an `[1,8,30,30]`
or differently-channeled output (it does not; 10-channel contract), or if cyan positions could be derived
without an F32 channel slice (they cannot without reading the input). Absent a scorer/contract change, 839
is the forced floor for every output family enumerated (Equal-tail one-hot, direct OneHot, U8 value canvas,
free-output multi-term Einsum).

## Don't-do log

Do not encode non-cyan cells as sentinel/empty inside the active output. ARC black `0` is a real output color and must set channel 0; only padding outside the compact `size x size` output is empty/all-zero. This was `task183_coloridx_einsum_3A17B461.onnx`, cost 966, visible 4/265.

Do not use rank-0 `OneHot` indices for the dynamic corner selector. ORT rejects it: `OneHot [ShapeInferenceError] Indices tensor must have rank >= 1`. Keep the index as `[1]` or use a different selector route.

Do not retry F16 on the `Einsum` selector as a free dtype win. Probe `task183_dtypeprobe_f16selector_0CA6AC39.onnx` is rejected by ORT: `Type parameter (T) of Optype (Einsum) bound to different types (tensor(float) and tensor(float16))`. Probe `task183_dtypeprobe_f16cyan_3C8118A2.onnx` is byte-equal but costs 1070.

Do not repeat the old `cast_after_first_slice` route without a semantic fix; prior OB_BIG log says it saved bytes but verified only 265/265.

Do not lower the graph to opset 12 just to use attribute-form `Unsqueeze`. Probe `task183_halfsize_novec_addactive_op12_18D208ED.onnx` scores `None` and ORT rejects it: `Type 'tensor(bool)' of input parameter (onehot6) of operator (Pad) is invalid`. Keep opset 13 for the Bool Pad tail.

Do not trust the `best_ext_cost=110` / `kmmmvs_local_best` state row as a floor counterexample. `data/competitor_artifacts/kmmmvs_local_best/submission/task183.onnx` is a one-node 1x1 Conv that scores `(0, 0, 110)` but verifies 0/265 vs expected and 0/265 vs LIVE. A local scan of `data/competitor_artifacts/**/task183.onnx` found no valid artifact below 853; the lower static-cost entries were 0/265 false leads.

Do not rely on sparse initializers as a scorer-visible discount for selector vectors. Sparse probes pass raw ORT smoke/A-B checks, but `score_network_v2` returns `None`: the sanitizer does not rename `graph.sparse_initializer`, and even pre-safe-name sparse graphs fail ONNX full shape inference on sparse `Einsum` inputs. Treat sparse as learn-only unless the scorer path changes.

Do not retry `UINT8`/narrow-int scalar `Sub` for the corner sums. ONNX schema for `Sub` at opset 13 only allows uint32/uint64/int32/int64/float16/float/double/bfloat16 here, and ORT rejects `task183_count_cornersum_u8scalar_082A6144.onnx` with `Type 'tensor(uint8)' ... is invalid`.

Do not move scalar `zero_u8`/`ten_u8` initializers to `Constant` nodes as a param dodge. Probe `task183_count_cornersum_const_u8_256CE75A.onnx` verifies on smoke but scores 843, worse than 841, because the constants are still charged and also add memory.

The opset-18 `Pad` axes trick has been fully exploited: `pad18_axes` cost 839 is the current best, achieving params=79 by splitting the 8-element `pads` into a 4-element `pads` + 2-element `axes`. No further params can be saved this way without a structural change to the Pad path.
